messages:
Maya (product): Quick planning thread: we need to lock launch criteria for dedicated capacity flow-control (reserved pools, quotas, burst windows, autoscale gating). Goals: predictable tail latency, clear customer expectations, fast operator controls. Who can help scope?

Leon (eng): I can. Main tradeoff: soft quotas reduce client errors but can hide noisy neighbors. We should define soft vs hard with concrete behavior.

Priya (eng-sre): Suggestion: soft = token-bucket throttling + short grace refunds; hard = immediate 429/over-limit. Add automatic fallback to compatible hosted/downgraded model on hard preempt. Metrics to watch: p95/p99 latency, queue depth, preempt_count/min, headroom_pct.

Carlos (sales): On the commercial side, customers want a simple contract: baseline reserved capacity + explicit burst best-effort. They expect a label they can sell to internal stakeholders (e.g., "Reserved Plus: X baseline, Y burst best-effort").

Mei (cs): Customers also ask for route-level guarantees. Example: chat routes should be protected; embeddings can be best-effort for cost reasons. Need per-route override in the API.

Leon (eng): Proposal for priorities: critical | standard | best-effort. Enforcement: critical eats reserved pool first, standard uses leftover, best-effort is evicted first. Implementation: tag requests with session_priority, maintain per-tenant token buckets, evict KV cache by priority then LRU.

Maya (product): For launch we need a minimal surface: API + Console config for reserved pool size + per-route priority, enforcement engine supporting soft/hard modes, tenant observability (headroom + preempt logs), and a pilot rollout plan. Anything else?

Priya (eng-sre): Operator features: manual drain/reassign reserved pools, quick evict command, and a canary flag per-tenant. Also add automatic fallback policy: route -> fallback_model or fallback_region.

Leon (eng): Example API snippet for opt-in soft quotas:```json
{"reserved_pool": {"reserved_gpus": 2}, "quota_mode": "soft", "route_priorities": {"/v1/chat": "critical", "/v1/embed": "best-effort"}}
```Soft mode = token bucket + 10s grace; hard mode = strict counters -> 429s.

Carlos (sales): Need to map that into product tiers and pricing. I'll propose two bundles: Reserved Lite (baseline + community burst) and Reserved SLA (baseline + guaranteed headroom + SLA on p95).

Mei (cs): Acceptance criteria from CS: successful onboarding of 3 pilot customers who exercise burst; runbook and support playbook validated; dashboard shows tenant-level burst and preempt events.

Maya (product): Draft launch checklist: 1) Spec PR with API + Console mocks, 2) Basic soft quotas + dashboard in v1, 3) Opt-in canary + pilot customers, 4) Runbook + operator UI, 5) Alerting rules (headroom < 10%, preempt_rate > 1/min), 6) Postmortem retro plan.

Leon (eng): Rough timeline: v1 (soft quotas + observability + pilot) in ~6 weeks if we pause per-route overrides; v2 (hard quotas, per-route enforced SLAs, pricing tie-ins) in next quarter.

Priya (eng-sre): Risks: noisy neighbors, unintended global throttles. Mitigation: feature flags, tenant canary, auto-fallback to hosted endpoints. We should also add a chaos test for preempt events during rollout.

Carlos (sales): I can get 2 pilot customers that accept soft quota semantics and gradual rollout. I'll draft comms about what "best-effort burst" means.

Maya (product): Action items: Leon -> spec PR + sample payloads; Priya -> runbook + operator UI mock + chaos tests; Carlos -> pilot commitments + pricing skus; Mei -> CS playbook + onboarding checklist. Sync Wed 11am to review spec.

deploy-bot: Heads up — open PRs touching capacity-control must include migration notes and schema changes. Branch protection enforced when spec PR is opened. :robot_face:
